Clean a corpus before encoding

Source: R/corpus.R
clean_corpus.Rd

clean_corpus() removes material without topical meaning from a corpus before encoding: markup, links, citation numbers, list markers, and broken characters. Text exported from web pages, databases, and documents carries such material; left in place, it shifts the embeddings, appears among the topic terms, and can form topics of its own. Cleaning the text once, before encoding, means that the encoder, the topic terms, and the representative texts all see the same clean text.

It always repairs broken characters and removes markup, links, e-mail addresses, DOIs, and bracketed citation numbers. It removes list markers and section numbering by default, and on request numbers, Roman numerals, and the matches of patterns of one's own (remove). Words, author citations, dates, decimals, and numbers within sentences are kept. Documents left empty, or with a share of letters below min_content (see content_ratio()), are dropped. For a data frame, the dropped rows are removed whole, so other columns stay aligned with the text. It returns the cleaned texts that are kept or, for a data frame, the kept rows with column cleaned.

The numbers, roman_numerals, and section_numbers arguments of topics(), by contrast, filter only the topic terms and leave the text unchanged.

Usage

clean_corpus(
  text,
  column = NULL,
  list_markers = TRUE,
  section_numbers = TRUE,
  numbers = FALSE,
  roman_numerals = FALSE,
  remove = NULL,
  min_content = 0
)

Arguments

text

A character vector, or a data frame together with column.

column

Name of the text column when text is a data frame; NULL (default) for a character vector.

list_markers

Remove list and enumeration markers (default TRUE); see strip_list_markers().

section_numbers

Remove section numbering such as 1.2.3 and II.2 (default TRUE).

numbers

Remove stand-alone numbers such as years and counts, keeping words with digits such as covid19 (default FALSE).

roman_numerals

Remove stand-alone Roman numerals of two or more letters, such as ii and xiv (default FALSE).

remove

Optional character vector of Perl-compatible regular expressions, matched case-insensitively; each match is replaced by a space. Default NULL.

min_content

Minimum share of letters for a document to be kept, between 0 and 1 (default 0, keep every non-empty document).

Value

For a character vector, the cleaned texts that are kept. For a data frame, the rows that are kept, with column cleaned.

Conditions

An error of class sbert_bad_input when column is given for a character vector.

See also

strip_list_markers() and content_ratio(), which it uses; dedupe() to collapse repeated texts after cleaning.

Examples

clean_corpus(c(
  "1. The directive entered into force in 2020.",
  "OJ No L 297, 24.11.1979, p. 1."
), min_content = 0.5)
#> [1] "The directive entered into force in 2020."

# Remove a reference form of one's own corpus
clean_corpus("as set out in OJ No L 313 it applies.",
             remove = "OJ No L?\\s*\\d+")
#> [1] "as set out in it applies."
